title: A Universal Entanglement Witness Generator
authors: Aiden R. Rosebush, Alexander C. B. Greenwood, Andi Shahaj, Li Qian
abstract: Entanglement witnesses are essential for certifying entanglement, yet constructing ones that are both noise-robust and economical in measurement settings remains challenging - particularly beyond qubits and for non-stabilizer ("magic") states. We present a machine-learning method that, given a target state and a user-specified number of measurement settings, generates an entanglement witness optimized for noise tolerance in the neighborhood of that state, requiring only local measurements. The approach is fully general, applying to multipartite qubit and qudit systems alike, including non-stabilizer states. For N qudits of dimension d, we train on the fully-separable eigenstates of each qudit's SU(d) generators to find a prototype witness, then tune the witness's bias term via gradient descent to maximize noise tolerance. Adversarial training further strengthens the witnesses, delivering greater noise tolerance with even fewer settings; critically, under this scheme the required training-set size becomes independent of system size. We package the entire pipeline as an automated script that, in every case we tested, produces witnesses surpassing all existing methods in noise tolerance and/or number of measurement settings. We demonstrate the method on Bell, GHZ, W, and hypergraph states, along with a range of qudit states, spanning 2-6 qubits, bipartite qudits up to d=10, and tripartite qutrits. Our witnesses achieve perfect accuracy across both physical experimental test states and large numerical sets of separable mixed states-including 30 million test states for a 3-qubit W-state witness and 10 million for a 4-qubit hypergraph-state witness-and we experimentally confirm the noise tolerance of Bell- and hypergraph state witnesses on both photonic and superconducting platforms, respectively.
summary: This paper introduces a universal machine-learning framework to generate highly robust entanglement witnesses for multipartite qubit and qudit systems. By optimizing witness construction using adversarial training, it overcomes limitations in measurement efficiency and noise tolerance compared to prior methods. This tool is vital for experimentally verifying genuine quantum entanglement across diverse physical platforms.
main_problem: The challenge is constructing entanglement witnesses that are simultaneously noise-robust, measurement-economical, and applicable to complex systems beyond simple qubits.
main_result: The authors propose a general machine-learning pipeline that generates superior entanglement witnesses with greater noise tolerance using fewer local measurements than existing methods.
method: A novel ML approach trains an entanglement witness by optimizing for noise tolerance via gradient descent and adversarial training, requiring only user-specified local measurement settings.
model_or_system: The method is general, applicable to multipartite qubit and qudit systems (d-level systems), including non-stabilizer states. It tests on various structured states like Bell, GHZ, W, and hypergraph states.
key_observables: Entanglement witnesses ($W$), noise tolerance parameter ($p$), expectation values ($\langle W angle$).
important_parameters: Number of qudits ($N$), dimension ($d$), user-specified number of measurement settings ($M$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the required training set size becomes independent of system size under adversarial training, and it aims to surpass existing methods' limitations regarding setting count.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes mention testing on various state types rather than describing figure content).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for robust witnesses, then details the ML framework involving prototype witness generation ($W_0$), refinement via differential programming to find $ho_s$, and finally strengthening it with adversarial training.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, automated tool for certifying entanglement in complex quantum systems, which is crucial for validating experimental results across various platforms (photonic/superconducting).

Shown are the counts of 3 million separable test states (in orange) Werner states based on the target W state up to the maximum noise tolerance of the witness (in blue). Notice the separable states have only positive expectation values, meeting the definition of an entanglement witness. Here we use 100 bins for each type of state, with a binsize of about 0.007.

FIG. 5. Experimental set up for (1) creating the noisy bipartite entangled photonic state (box 1); (2) adding noise to the entangled state (box 2); and (3) local projective measurements on each photon (box 3). We then combined the signal and the noise with a 50/50 splitter, put the total signal through a Pump Suppression Filter (PSF) before separating the C and L band components for measurement. We used Polarization Analyzers (PAs) consisting of a quarter waveplate, and a half waveplate to project the photons onto the polarizer before the single photon detectors.
